rail_guard.text: Snowdon Mountain Railway, the only rack railway in Britain. Mind the teeth.

pryce_quarry.text: Good afternoon. Gareth Pryce, Regional Director for Wales. You'll have received my email. You haven't? How odd, it was copied to everyone.
The quarry is, as of Tuesday, a Licensed Heritage Asset. You are currently an unlicensed visitor. There is a form.
I'm told battles are the quickest way to resolve a dispute. I have scheduled one. It is on the agenda, item four.
I shall be escalating this to the Yr Wyddfa office. I believe you will find that office to be on top of a mountain.
The quarry gates are open, as a gesture. It is a very small gesture. Do not frame it.
Sir, you have left your lanyard in the quarry.
Leave it. It is, strictly, a tactical retreat.

then.text: Cloud on the summit. The train still goes up. You won't see much, but you'll see it sitting down.
Too windy at the top today, so we're stopping short. The mountain is in charge, not the timetable.

porter.text: The Snowdon Mountain Railway opened in 1896. It's a rack and pinion line, so the train grips the track with teeth.
Four and a half miles to the summit. Takes an hour. Walkers say we cheat. We say we sit down.

lake_angler.text: Llyn Padarn has a fish you'll hardly find anywhere else in Britain: the torgoch, or Arctic char. Red belly.
I've not caught one. I've caught a lot of reeds.

castle_guide.text: Dolbadarn Castle: Prince Llywelyn the Great's round tower, built around 1230. One tower, lots of staircase.
The roof is missing. The staircase is, frankly, optional.

then.text: Rain on slate, best sound there is. Means the roof's doing its job.
See the quarry in the sun? All that slate shining like a staircase for giants.

slate_veteran.text: Dinorwic closed in 1969. Thousands worked there, in all weathers, on galleries cut into the hill.
Slate roofs from here are on houses in Hamburg and Australia. Wales: exporting rain protection since forever.

then.text: Have you seen the wood by the park? Proper rainforest now. Gwen comes in for her bara brith dripping wet and grinning like a lamb.
Glaw eto. Rain again. Come in, there's a pot of te on and the cacen is still warm.
Can't see Yr Wyddfa today. She's shy. Have a slice of bara brith while she makes her mind up.

else.text: Te? Coffi? Cacen? Say it with me. It means tea, coffee, cake. In that order of priority.
We also do a full Welsh breakfast, a rare treat. It comes with laverbread. Try it, or don't.

then.text: It's raining, which is fine, because Scouts are always prepared. I'm prepared to get wet.
It's getting dark, so Akela says we have to go back. I wasn't scared of the giant's grave. Much.

scout_kid.text: {greeting} I'm earning my 'walked up Snowdon' badge. I did half. The train did the other half.
Yr Wyddfa means 'the burial mound'. A giant's grave, they say. Rather big for a gravestone.

gate_cambrian.text: The road south is closed. Heritage Assessment. We're waiting for Director Pryce to come back with the results.
He's been up the mountain for a while. I'm sure it's going very well.

then.text: If you're thinking of going up Yr Wyddfa, I wouldn't. I'd stay down here. With the barrier. It's quite nice.

llan_skimmer.text: Llyn Padarn is the best stone-skimming lake in Wales, and I will fight anyone who says Bala. Carreg is a stone, by the way. Cerrig, plural. You will need plenty.
